title: A $6.6 million nursing contract began months after two State citations, both under appeal

beats.text: 6,610,689 dollars.

visual.label: agreed on a Public Health skilled-nursing contract

beats.text: A Public Health contract for skilled-nursing beds, begun 1 July 2026.

visual.label: agreed on a Public Health skilled-nursing contract

beats.text: The operator: Garfield Nursing Home Inc, licensee of two homes, in Oakland and Cherryland.
This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: Seven months before it began, the State cited the operator’s Oakland home.

visual.text: Class AA citation at Garfield Neurobehavioral Center, $75,000, under appeal

beats.text: The first lead.
Two citations at Garfield Neurobehavioral Center: class A in October 2025, 25,000 dollars.
Then class AA in November, 75,000 dollars.
These are the State’s two costliest classes. Class B’s middle penalty is 3,000 dollars.
But both are open and under appeal. Neither has been upheld.

visual.line: each appealed and each still open

beats.text: All three notices charge abuse of a resident. All three are under appeal.

visual.kicker: Class AA, A and B notices: events of 2024 and 2025

beats.text: The appeals were received in November and December 2025. The State’s counts give no outcome yet.
The second lead.

visual.text: Purchasing authority: Behavioral Health and Residential Care Contracts by DPH
visual.mark: Behavioral Health and Residential Care Contracts by DPH

beats.text: Contract 1000038024 ran through a route where an ordinance waives competitive bidding.

visual.text: Purchasing authority: Behavioral Health and Residential Care Contracts by DPH
visual.mark: Behavioral Health and Residential Care Contracts by DPH

beats.text: Its term began seven months after the class AA citation, and eight after the class A.
A contract that is not bid is never priced against another operator.

steps.name: Bidding waived
steps.sub: Behavioral Health and Residential Care Contracts by DPH

beats.text: The department’s own review is the only check. Did it see the citations? The files don’t say.

steps.name: Bidding waived
steps.sub: Behavioral Health and Residential Care Contracts by DPH

beats.text: Public Health’s June 2026 summary to the Health Commission doesn’t mention them.

visual.text: City clients filled an average of 21 beds over the past year: 15 at Garfield Neurobehavioral Center and 6 at Morton Bakar Center

beats.text: It says 15 of 21 City beds were at Garfield, the home cited.

visual.text: City clients filled an average of 21 beds over the past year: 15 at Garfield Neurobehavioral Center and 6 at Morton Bakar Center

beats.text: It asks 8,925,337 dollars, more than the contract table. The files don’t say why.
The same day, Public Health began a contract with a different operator, Medical Hill Healthcare Center.

visual.label: paid by Public Health so far

beats.text: No earlier payment shows under its name: earlier beds were paid through a check-writing contract.

visual.line: previously managed under the HR360 check writing contract

beats.text: The fourth lead. Related companies owed the two homes a net 55.4 million dollars.

visual.label: owed to the two homes by related companies, 2025

beats.text: That’s against 27,693,214 dollars of revenue in 2025.
It’s money the homes have earned and do not hold. Common where a chain pools cash.

beats.text: What would settle it? The outcome of the appeals, and the contract’s waiver and award file.

beats.text: Both citations are under appeal. The question is what Public Health knew when it signed.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
